sections.html:
Belton is the seat of Bell County in Central Texas, and it keeps getting bigger. It had 18,216 residents in 2010 and 23,054 in 2020. Counting from the 2020 estimates base, the July 1, 2025 figure of 25,964 is up 12.7%. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $258,700, and owners live in 56.0% of the homes. Tenants pay about $1,252 a month at the median, which makes rentals a sizable part of the local market.

Steady demand helps, but a seller still has a tax bill to square away, maybe a tenant to deal with, and a deed to sign. The sections below cover Belton details first and the Texas rules after them. Owners of older lots near Nolan Creek should check floodplain status before listing, since lenders ask.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and early-payment discounts
sections.html:
Bell CAD appraises property and also takes the payments. One statement for the whole year goes out each October. Payment is due when it arrives, and a balance left after January 31 starts drawing penalties on February 1. A full early payment earns a discount from certain taxing entities, as shown below.

Bell CAD payment timing for a full-year bill
Payment monthDiscount for paying in full
October3%
November2%
December1%
JanuaryBase tax, no discount and no penalty
February 1 onwardPenalties begin
  • Payment options include online, phone, or a visit to a district office.
  • The Belton office has a drop box outside for after-hours payments.
  • Deferral, quarterly installment and homestead delinquent installment agreements are explained on the district's site.

Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. Sales and properties get a fresh look each year, so a value can shift from one notice to the next. Tuck your newest notice into the closing folder, as buyers will want to see the figure the house carries.

Filing opens January 1 and closes April 30, at the district office or online. After approval the exemption carries forward by itself. Renewal comes up only if the chief appraiser sends a request or you change homes. Bell CAD will also accept a late filing for two years after the tax goes delinquent.

To qualify, you must have lived in the house as your residence on January 1, with no other homestead claimed. State law caps the land at 20 acres, but the district describes an acre or less as the usual case. A mobile home owner on rented land can still apply, using a title or a verified purchase contract.

Older and disabled owners get extra relief, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or over can keep the school tax ceiling. A disabled veteran submits a VA letter showing a rating of 10% or higher, and 100% may support a full exemption on the homestead.

sections.h2: Does the 10% homestead cap change what a buyer pays?
sections.html:
The cap touches assessed value only. Market value moves with sales and has no ceiling, but a homestead's assessment can grow only 10% per year. That protection begins after the owner has held the home through one full January 1.

A buyer paying far above the old assessment may see the bill rise for several years while the assessment works up to market value. A buyer who will live there should hear that from you.

The ordinance on short-term rentals dates to March 13, 2023. Each rental carries a one-year city permit, and the owner has 30 days from expiration to apply for renewal. Unpaid local hotel and motel occupancy tax blocks the renewal.

A rental the owner doesn't occupy must stay at least 500 feet from another short-term rental. Every address needs a separate application in the online portal, where income is also reported each quarter, with zero entered for months without guests.

  • The city's portal handles applications and renewals.
  • Planning Department staff can explain the process.

If the house was a rental, finish the tax filings before closing so nothing follows you afterward.

sections.h2: Tenants in the house before closing
sections.html:
Any Texas eviction begins with a written notice to vacate, and the default is three days unless the lease sets another period. A landlord may hand it over, leave it inside the unit, mail it, or email it if the lease allows.

A tenant who stays can be taken to justice court, where the hearing falls 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeals to county court must be made within five days of the judgment. A writ of possession can follow after six days, and removal comes with 24 hours of warning. Plan your closing date around that schedule, or sell with the tenant staying on.

Many Texas loans give the lender a power of sale, so the house goes to a courthouse auction held on a first Tuesday. You have 20 days after the default letter to reinstate the loan. Notice of the sale then has to reach you at least 21 days before the auction. An owner who can't catch up often does best by selling beforehand and keeping the equity.

Property tax works separately. Its lien attaches each January 1 and rides with the land through any sale. Because the January 1 owner stays liable, the title company should clear that year's bill at the closing table.

sections.h2: Where a Belton deed is filed
sections.html:
You record a deed for Bell County land with the county clerk, after it has been signed and acknowledged. Once it is on file, ask Bell CAD what it needs to update the owner name on the account.

The state clerk manual puts the recording fee at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every page after it, plus other statutory charges. Call the clerk for the exact total. Usually the title company files it and sends you a copy.

Listing the house means showings, a buyer's mortgage, an appraisal and repair requests after the inspection. A cash sale cuts most of that out, so clear title mostly sets the pace. Ask for any offer in writing, then have the title company check the tax payoff, any liens and who must sign the deed.

Before you ask for offers, collect your latest tax statement and appraisal notice, a mortgage payoff figure if there is a loan, any lease or rental permit papers, and notes on floodplain or repair history. A buyer with that folder can price the house fast.

On closing day the title company settles the year's property tax, pays off the mortgage, and records the deed with the Bell County clerk. If a tenant is staying, say so in the contract. If the house ran as a short-term rental, show that the city tax filings are current. Both tend to draw last-minute questions from buyers.

faqs.q: When must a Belton homestead application be filed?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 30 of the tax year. Bell CAD takes late filings for two years after the tax turns delinquent, and the exemption needs no yearly renewal.

faqs.q: Is there an early-pay discount on Belton property tax?
faqs.a: For certain taxing entities, yes: 3% off in October, 2% in November and 1% in December. January is the base amount.

faqs.q: Can I rent a Belton house on a nightly basis?
faqs.a: Only if the city issues a permit, renewed each year. A rental where the owner doesn't live must be 500 feet from any other short-term rental.

faqs.q: If I sell a Belton house mid-year, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: Whoever owned it on January 1 holds the lien and the liability. The title company normally splits the bill between seller and buyer at closing.

faqs.q: Which office values my Belton house?
faqs.a: Bell CAD, which keeps offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple and looks at sales and properties each year.
